It's been a year since we showed the problem of pollution from sewage entering the Vaal -- now The Vaal River is experiencing some of its worst pollution to date, form the same source

Unique Selling Point:
At present there are two 'hotspots' - Vereeniging, Three Rivers, where a pump station is overflowing.
This is near the Bon Hotel and Riviera villas in Mario Milani Drive which runs parallel to the river.
The second is the Rietsprut.
There are huge amounts of foam flowing in the Rietspruit and SAVE the VAAL is not getting answers as to the source of this pollution.

Press Release:


It's been a year since Carte Blanche highlighted the problem of pollution from sewage entering the Vaal River system. Attempts were made to rectify the problem, but it seems the River is currently experiencing some of its worst pollution to date. Good work or a dismal failure?

Script:


SCRIPT: Vaal Report Card
PRODUCERS: Marzanne van den Berg & Anna-Maria van Niekerk
PRESENTER: Claire Mawisa
TX DATE: 8 October 2017

The Vaal River and Dam make life possible in the northern half of South Africa - it’s the water source for millions of people and industries. Last month, it saw some of the worst pollution to date - e.coli counts spiked at 1.2 million per 100 milliliters … 400 already spells danger.

CLAIRE LINK: E. coli shows that there’s raw sewage in the water. This bacteria in our water can make people and animals very sick with gastrointestinal diseases and skin irritation.

Malcolm Plant chairs Save the Vaal Environment - an group of unpaid activists who live and work on the Vaal.

CLAIRE MAWISA: What are those health risks that you have identified?

MALCOLM PLANT, CHAIRPERSON, SAVE THE VAAL ENVIRONMENT: ...your green algae in the water, the stink, the raw sewerage that’s running around in the rivers itself which then flows through complexes...the local kids swim in the little estuaries, the small rivers. They use the water to grow their own vegetables. So all the water that they’re using is actually raw sewerage water that they’re actually putting back into their own bodies.

It’s school holidays - the river should be bustling … but it’s quiet. The worst of the sewage spill has washed downstream by now. River estate manager Kas Lubbe has seen the problem return time and again.

KAS LUBBE, ESTATE MANAGER: The smell is unbearable. If you try to sit next to the river, this beautiful place, you can see solids flowing into the river. It turns your stomach.

We’ve returned repeatedly since 2015 to check on the state of the Vaal. In July there was good news -- work had begun on the upgrade of treatment works in Deneysville next to the dam. Downstream in Vereeniging, things remain dire.

KAS LUBBE, ESTATE MANAGER: Raw sewage is pumped into the river regularly. Whenever something went wrong, they switch this pump station off… when they worked on the system somewhere. The water just overflows, go into the storm water system and flows directly into the Vaal River.

This was in September. The telltale white foam indicates the presence of sewage. A pump station in Vereeniging was again the hotspot.

CLAIRE MAWISA: Why are there hotspots?

MALCOLM PLANT, CHAIRPERSON, SAVE THE VAAL ENVIRONMENT: The hotspots are caused from spillages, breakdown in the networks and also from Eskom failures. They also have a huge problem with vandalism at all the pump stations.

Treatment works often run over capacity, and effluent cannot be treated to standard. Last year, Water and Sanitation Department spokesman Sputnik Ratau blamed municipalities.

SPUTNIK RATAU, SPOKESPERSON, DEPARTMENT OF WATER AND SANITATION: That is where you find even if there was infrastructure initially but after a while the quality starts being impacted upon.

In the crossfire is Emfuleni Local Municipality, comprising Vereeniging and Vanderbijlpark, where much of Gauteng’s sewage is treated.

KAS LUBBE, ESTATE MANAGER: There’s guys that really try their best to do something but you can see that their hands are tied with money and so on.

CLAIRE LINK: The Emfuleni municipality said that 50 new pumps and pipes have been bought and these are currently being installed to replace old infrastructure. It deals with spillages as they occur.

The municipality earns a D for effort.

UPS KAS LUBBE (pointing to pump station 10): It’s running.

CLAIRE LINK: Even when local systems fail, the National Department of Water and Sanitation remains responsible for protecting our water.

Hopes were pinned on the Sedibeng Regional Sewer Scheme, a project backed by national government that would see existing infrastructure upgraded and a mega works built. But last year funds were rerouted to the higher education crisis.

MALCOLM PLANT, CHAIRPERSON, SAVE THE VAAL ENVIRONMENT: The SRSS was announced in 2003, which was then put on hold, nothing ever happened with the system.

CLAIRE LINK: Emfuleni told us that the future of the Sedibeng Regional Sewer Scheme will be discussed this month with Rand Water and the Departments of Water and Sanitation and Cooperative Governance.

The Department did not respond to our questions. It scores an F, as lasting solutions seem far off.


PROMOS
10 secs
Sewage has spilled into the Vaal River again. What is government doing to protect this key water resource for billions of people?

15 secs
It’s a major water source in Gauteng so why are e. coli levels spiking dangerously in the Vaal River?
KAS LUBBE, ESTATE MANAGER: The smell is unbearable. If you try to sit next to the river, this beautiful place … you can see solids floating in the river. It turns your stomach.

15 secs
Sewage systems in densely populated Gauteng are spilling waste into the precious Vaal River -- where’s the mega works that was meant to be built?
MALCOLM PLANT, CHAIRPERSON, SAVE THE VAAL ENVIRONMENT: The SRSS was announced in 2003, which was then put on hold, nothing ever happened...
